{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/.claude/skills/frontend-playbook\n\n# Frontend Playbook\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"I'll use `yarn chain`.\"** Wrong. `yarn chain` gives you an empty local chain with no protocols, no tokens, no state. `yarn fork --network base` gives you a copy of real Base with Uniswap, Aave, USDC, real whale balances — everything (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`). Always fork.\n\n**\"I deployed to IPFS and it works.\"** Did the CID change? If not, you deployed stale output. Did routes work? Without `trailingSlash: true`, every route except `/` returns 404. Did you check the OG image? Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL`, it points to `localhost:3000`.\n\n**\"I'll set up the project manually.\"** Don't. `npx create-eth@latest` handles everything — Foundry, Next.js, RainbowKit, scaffold hooks. Never run `forge init` or create Next.js projects from scratch.\n\n---\n\n## Fork Mode Setup\n\n### Why Fork, Not Chain\n\n```\nyarn chain (WRONG)              yarn fork --network base (CORRECT)\n└─ Empty local chain            └─ Fork of real Base mainnet\n└─ No protocols                 └─ Uniswap, Aave, etc. available\n└─ No tokens                    └─ Real USDC, WETH exist\n└─ Testing in isolation         └─ Test against REAL state\n```\n\n### Setup\n\n```bash\nnpx create-eth@latest          # Select: foundry, target chain, name\ncd <project-name>\nyarn install\nyarn fork --network base       # Terminal 1: fork of real Base\nyarn deploy                    # Terminal 2: deploy contracts to fork\nyarn start                     # Terminal 3: Next.js frontend\n```\n\n### Critical: Chain ID Gotcha\n\n**When using fork mode, the frontend target network MUST be `chains.foundry` (chain ID 31337), NOT the chain you're forking.**\n\nThe fork runs locally on Anvil with chain ID 31337. Even if you're forking Base:\n\n```typescript\n// scaffold.config.ts during development\ntargetNetworks: [chains.foundry],  // ✅ NOT chains.base!\n```\n\nOnly switch to `chains.base` when deploying contracts to the REAL network.\n\n### Enable Block Mining\n\n```bash\n# In a new terminal — REQUIRED for time-dependent logic\ncast rpc anvil_setIntervalMining 1\n```\n\nWithout this, `block.timestamp` stays FROZEN. Any contract logic using timestamps (deadlines, expiry, vesting) will break silently.\n\n**Make it permanent** by editing `packages/foundry/package.json` to add `--block-time 1` to the fork script.\n\n---\n\n## Deploying to IPFS (Recommended)\n\nIPFS is the recommended deploy path for SE2. Avoids Vercel's memory limits entirely. Produces a fully decentralized static site.\n\n### Full Build Command\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nrm -rf .next out  # ALWAYS clean first\n\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://yourapp.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Upload to BuidlGuidl IPFS\nyarn bgipfs upload out\n# Save the CID!\n```\n\n### Node 25+ localStorage Polyfill (REQUIRED)\n\nNode.js 25+ ships a built-in `localStorage` object that's MISSING standard WebStorage API methods (`getItem`, `setItem`). This breaks `next-themes`, RainbowKit, and any library that calls `localStorage.getItem()` during static page generation.\n\n**Error you'll see:**\n```\nTypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function\nError occurred prerendering page \"/_not-found\"\n```\n\n**The fix:** Create `polyfill-localstorage.cjs` in `packages/nextjs/`:\n```javascript\nif (typeof globalThis.localStorage !== \"undefined\" &&\n    typeof globalThis.localStorage.getItem !== \"function\") {\n  const store = new Map();\n  globalThis.localStorage = {\n    getItem: (key) => store.get(key) ?? null,\n    setItem: (key, value) => store.set(key, String(value)),\n    removeItem: (key) => store.delete(key),\n    clear: () => store.clear(),\n    key: (index) => [...store.keys()][index] ?? null,\n    get length() { return store.size; },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n**Why `--require` and not `instrumentation.ts`?** Next.js spawns a separate build worker process for prerendering. `--require` injects into EVERY Node process (including workers). `next.config.ts` polyfill only runs in the main process. `instrumentation.ts` doesn't run in the build worker. Only `--require` works.\n\n### IPFS Routing — Why Routes Break\n\nIPFS gateways serve static files. No server handles routing. Three things MUST be true:\n\n**1. `output: \"export\"` in next.config.ts** — generates static HTML files.\n\n**2. `trailingSlash: true` (CRITICAL)** — This is the #1 reason routes break:\n- `trailingSlash: false` (default) → generates `debug.html`\n- `trailingSlash: true` → generates `debug/index.html`\n- IPFS gateways resolve directories to `index.html` automatically, but NOT bare filenames\n- Without trailing slash: `/debug` → 404 ❌\n- With trailing slash: `/debug` → `debug/` → `debug/index.html` ✅\n\n**3. Pages must survive static prerendering** — any page that crashes during `yarn build` (browser APIs at import time, localStorage) gets skipped silently → 404 on IPFS.\n\n**The complete IPFS-safe next.config.ts pattern:**\n```typescript\nconst isIpfs = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD === \"true\";\nif (isIpfs) {\n  nextConfig.output = \"export\";\n  nextConfig.trailingSlash = true;\n  nextConfig.images = { unoptimized: true };\n}\n```\n\n**SE2's block explorer pages** use `localStorage` at import time and crash during static export. Rename `app/blockexplorer` to `app/_blockexplorer-disabled` if not needed.\n\n### Stale Build Detection\n\n**The #1 IPFS footgun:** You edit code, then deploy the OLD build.\n\n```bash\n# MANDATORY after ANY code change:\nrm -rf .next out                     # 1. Delete old artifacts\n# ... run full build command ...     # 2. Rebuild from scratch\ngrep -l \"YOUR_STRING\" out/_next/static/chunks/app/*.js  # 3. Verify changes present\n\n# Timestamp check:\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx           # Source modified time\nstat -f '%Sm' out/                   # Build output time\n# Source NEWER than out/ = STALE BUILD. Rebuild first!\n```\n\n**The CID is proof:** If the IPFS CID didn't change after a deploy, you deployed the same content. A real code change ALWAYS produces a new CID.\n\n### Verify Routes After Deploy\n\n```bash\nls out/*/index.html                  # Each route has a directory + index.html\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" -L \"https://GATEWAY/ipfs/CID/debug/\"\n# Should return 200, not 404\n```\n\n---\n\n## Deploying to Vercel (Alternative)\n\nSE2 is a monorepo — Vercel needs special configuration.\n\n### Configuration\n\n1. **Root Directory:** `packages/nextjs`\n2. **Install Command:** `cd ../.. && yarn install`\n3. **Build Command:** leave default (`next build`)\n4. **Output Directory:** leave default (`.next`)\n\n```bash\n# Via API:\ncurl -X PATCH \"https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/PROJECT_ID\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"rootDirectory\": \"packages/nextjs\", \"installCommand\": \"cd ../.. && yarn install\"}'\n```\n\n### Common Failures\n\n| Error | Cause | Fix |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| \"No Next.js version detected\" | Root Directory not set | Set to `packages/nextjs` |\n| \"cd packages/nextjs: No such file\" | Build command has `cd` | Clear it — root dir handles this |\n| OOM / exit code 129 | SE2 monorepo exceeds 8GB | Use IPFS instead, or `vercel --prebuilt` |\n\n### Decision Tree\n\n```\nWant to deploy SE2?\n├─ IPFS (recommended) → yarn ipfs / manual build + upload\n│   └─ Fully decentralized, no memory limits, works with ENS\n├─ Vercel → Set rootDirectory + installCommand\n│   └─ Fast CDN, but centralized. May OOM on large projects\n└─ vercel --prebuilt → Build locally, push artifacts to Vercel\n    └─ Best of both: local build power + Vercel CDN\n```\n\n---\n\n## ENS Subdomain Setup\n\nTwo mainnet transactions to point an ENS subdomain at your IPFS deployment.\n\n### Transaction 1: Create Subdomain (new apps only)\n\n1. Open `https://app.ens.domains/yourname.eth`\n2. Go to \"Subnames\" tab → \"New subname\"\n3. Enter the label (e.g. `myapp`) → Next → Skip profile → Open Wallet → Confirm\n4. If gas is stuck: switch MetaMask to Ethereum → Activity tab → \"Speed up\"\n\n### Transaction 2: Set IPFS Content Hash\n\n1. Navigate to `https://app.ens.domains/myapp.yourname.eth`\n2. \"Records\" tab → \"Edit Records\" → \"Other\" tab\n3. Paste in Content Hash field: `ipfs://<CID>`\n4. Save → Open Wallet → Confirm in MetaMask\n\nFor **updates** to an existing app: skip Tx 1, only do Tx 2.\n\n### Verify\n\n```bash\n# 1. Onchain content hash matches\nRESOLVER=$(cast call 0x00000000000C2e074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e \\\n  \"resolver(bytes32)(address)\" $(cast namehash myapp.yourname.eth) \\\n  --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com)\ncast call $RESOLVER \"contenthash(bytes32)(bytes)\" \\\n  $(cast namehash myapp.yourname.eth) --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com\n\n# 2. Gateway responds (may take 5-15 min for cache)\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" -L \"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\"\n\n# 3. OG metadata correct (not localhost)\ncurl -s -L \"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\" | grep 'og:image'\n```\n\n**Use `.eth.link` NOT `.eth.limo`** — `.eth.link` works better on mobile.\n\n---\n\n## Go to Production — Complete Checklist\n\nWhen the user says \"ship it\", follow this EXACT sequence.\n\n### Step 1: Final Code Review 🤖\n- All feedback incorporated\n- No duplicate h1, no raw addresses, no shared isLoading\n- `scaffold.config.ts` has `rpcOverrides` and `pollingInterval: 3000`\n\n### Step 2: Choose Domain 👤\nAsk: *\"What subdomain do you want? e.g. `myapp.yourname.eth` → `myapp.yourname.eth.link`\"*\n\n### Step 3: Generate OG Image + Fix Metadata 🤖\n- Create 1200×630 PNG (`public/thumbnail.png`) — NOT the stock SE2 thumbnail\n- Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` to the live domain\n- Verify `og:image` will resolve to an absolute production URL\n\n### Step 4: Clean Build + IPFS Deploy 🤖\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs && rm -rf .next out\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Verify before uploading:\nls out/*/index.html                        # Routes exist\ngrep 'og:image' out/index.html             # Not localhost\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx                 # Source older than out/\nstat -f '%Sm' out/\n\nyarn bgipfs upload out                     # Save the CID\n```\n\n### Step 5: Share for Approval 👤\nSend: *\"Build ready for review: `https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>`\"*\n**Wait for approval before touching ENS.**\n\n### Step 6: Set ENS 🤖\nCreate subdomain (if new) + set IPFS content hash. Two mainnet transactions.\n\n### Step 7: Verify 🤖\n- Content hash matches onchain\n- `.eth.link` gateway responds with 200\n- OG image loads correctly\n- Routes work (`/debug/`, etc.)\n\n### Step 8: Report 👤\n*\"Live at `https://myapp.yourname.eth.link` — ENS content hash confirmed onchain, unfurl metadata set.\"*\n\n---\n\n## Build Verification Process\n\nA build is NOT done when the code compiles. It's done when you've tested it like a real user.\n\n### Phase 1: Code QA (Automated)\n- Scan `.tsx` files for raw address strings (should use `<Address/>`)\n- Scan for shared `isLoading` state across multiple buttons\n- Scan for missing `disabled` props on transaction buttons\n- Verify RPC config and polling interval\n- Verify OG metadata with absolute URLs\n- Verify no public RPCs in any file\n\n### Phase 2: Smart Contract Testing\n```bash\nforge test                    # All tests pass\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000  # Fuzz testing\n```\nTest edge cases: zero amounts, max amounts, unauthorized callers, reentrancy attempts.\n\n### Phase 3: Browser Testing (THE REAL TEST)\n\nOpen the app and do a FULL walkthrough:\n\n1. **Load the app** — does it render correctly?\n2. **Check page title** — is it correct, not \"Scaffold-ETH 2\"?\n3. **Connect wallet** — does the connect flow work?\n4. **Wrong network** — connect on wrong chain, verify \"Switch to Base\" appears\n5. **Switch network** — click the switch button, verify it works\n6. **Approve flow** — verify approve button shows, click it, wait for tx, verify action button appears\n7. **Main action** — click primary action, verify loader, wait for tx, verify state updates\n8. **Error handling** — reject a transaction in wallet, verify UI recovers\n9. **Address displays** — all addresses showing ENS/blockies, not raw hex?\n10. **Share URL** — check OG unfurl (image, title, description)\n\n### Phase 4: QA Sub-Agent (Complex Builds)\nFor bigger projects, spawn a sub-agent with fresh context. Give it the repo path and deployed URL. It reads all code against the UX rules, opens a browser, clicks through independently, and reports issues.\n\n---\n\n## Don't Do These\n\n- ❌ `yarn chain` — use `yarn fork --network <chain>`\n- ❌ `forge init` — use `npx create-eth@latest`\n- ❌ Manual Next.js setup — SE2 handles it\n- ❌ Manual wallet connection — SE2 has RainbowKit pre-configured\n- ❌ Edit `deployedContracts.ts` — it's auto-generated by `yarn deploy`\n- ❌ Hardcode API keys in `scaffold.config.ts` — use `.env.local`\n- ❌ Use `mainnet.base.org` in production — use Alchemy or similar\n\n---\n\n## Resources\n\n- **SE2 Docs:** https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/\n- **UI Components:** https://ui.scaffoldeth.io/\n- **SpeedRun Ethereum:** https://speedrunethereum.com/\n- **ETH Tech Tree:** https://www.ethtechtree.com\n- **BuidlGuidl IPFS:** https://upload.bgipfs.com\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"f10a15ac-dcc7-459d-9ea0-f75506f03a18","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:54:19.841Z","isSynthetic":true}

Remove when deploying to a live network.\nimport \"forge-std/console.sol\";\n\n// Use openzeppelin to inherit battle-tested implementations (ERC20, ERC721, etc)\n// import \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\n\n/**\n * A smart contract that allows changing a state variable of the contract and tracking the changes\n * It also allows the owner to withdraw the Ether in the contract\n * @author BuidlGuidl\n */\ncontract YourContract {\n  // State Variables\n  address public immutable owner;\n  string public greeting = \"Building Unstoppable Apps!!!\";\n  bool public premium = false;\n  uint256 public totalCounter = 0;\n  mapping(address => uint256) public userGreetingCounter;\n\n  // Events: a way to emit log statements from smart contract that can be listened to by external parties\n  event GreetingChange(\n    address indexed greetingSetter,\n    string newGreeting,\n    bool premium,\n    uint256 value\n  );\n\n  // Constructor: Called once on contract deployment\n  // Check packages/foundry/deploy/Deploy.s.sol\n  constructor(address _owner) {\n    owner = _owner;\n  }\n\n  // Modifier: used to define a set of rules that must be met before or after a function is executed\n  // Check the withdraw() function\n  modifier isOwner() {\n    // msg.sender: predefined variable that represents address of the account that called the current function\n    require(msg.sender == owner, \"Not the Owner\");\n    _;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows anyone to change the state variable \"greeting\" of the contract and increase the counters\n   *\n   * @param _newGreeting (string memory) - new greeting to save on the contract\n   */\n  function setGreeting(string memory _newGreeting) public payable {\n    // Print data to the anvil chain console. Remove when deploying to a live network.\n\n    console.logString(\"Setting new greeting\");\n    console.logString(_newGreeting);\n\n    greeting = _newGreeting;\n    totalCounter += 1;\n    userGreetingCounter[msg.sender] += 1;\n\n    // msg.value: built-in global variable that represents the amount of ether sent with the transaction\n    if (msg.value > 0) {\n      premium = true;\n    } else {\n      premium = false;\n    }\n\n    // emit: keyword used to trigger an event\n    emit GreetingChange(msg.sender, _newGreeting, msg.value > 0, msg.value);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows the owner to withdraw all the Ether in the contract\n   * The function can only be called by the owner of the contract as defined by the isOwner modifier\n   */\n  function withdraw() public isOwner {\n    (bool success,) = owner.call{ value: address(this).balance }(\"\");\n    require(success, \"Failed to send Ether\");\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows the contract to receive ETH\n   */\n  receive() external payable { }\n}\n","numLines":85,"startLine":1,"totalLines":85}}}

Please use the object parameter version instead.\",\n      );\n    }\n  }, [configOrName]);\n  const { contractName, chainId } = finalConfig;\n  const selectedNetwork = useSelectedNetwork(chainId);\n  const deployedContract = contracts?.[selectedNetwork.id]?.[contractName as ContractName] as Contract<TContractName>;\n  const [status, setStatus] = useState<ContractCodeStatus>(ContractCodeStatus.LOADING);\n  const publicClient = usePublicClient({ chainId: selectedNetwork.id });\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const checkContractDeployment = async () => {\n      try {\n        if (!isMounted() || !publicClient) return;\n\n        if (!deployedContract) {\n          setStatus(ContractCodeStatus.NOT_FOUND);\n          return;\n        }\n\n        const code = await publicClient.getBytecode({\n          address: deployedContract.address,\n        });\n\n        // If contract code is `0x` => no contract deployed on that address\n        if (code === \"0x\") {\n          setStatus(ContractCodeStatus.NOT_FOUND);\n          return;\n===useScaffoldContract===\nimport { Account, Address, Chain, Client, Transport, getContract } from \"viem\";\nimport { usePublicClient } from \"wagmi\";\nimport { GetWalletClientReturnType } from \"wagmi/actions\";\nimport { useSelectedNetwork } from \"~~/hooks/scaffold-eth\";\nimport { useDeployedContractInfo } from \"~~/hooks/scaffold-eth\";\nimport { AllowedChainIds } from \"~~/utils/scaffold-eth\";\nimport { Contract, ContractName } from \"~~/utils/scaffold-eth/contract\";\n\n/**\n * Gets a viem instance of the contract present in deployedContracts.ts or externalContracts.ts corresponding to\n * targetNetworks configured in scaffold.config.ts. {\n            public: Client<Transport, Chain>;\n            wallet: TWalletClient;\n          }\n        : { public: Client<Transport, Chain> },\n      Chain,\n      Account\n    >({\n      address: deployedContractData.address,\n      abi: deployedContractData.abi as Contract<TContractName>[\"abi\"],\n      client: {\n        public: publicClient,\n        wallet: walletClient ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMEgb2VXxYjz4jJjgPNG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QKnqczQQyZHQKTs6dFhZD2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol","content":"//SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity >=0.8.0 <0.9.0;\n\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { SafeERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\n\n/**\n * A tip jar that accepts USDC tips with an optional public message and keeps an on-chain feed.\n * The USDC token address is fixed at deploy time: Base USDC in production, and the exact same\n * address on a `yarn fork --network base` fork, so local demos hit the real USDC contract.\n * @author BuidlGuidl\n */\ncontract TipJar {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    struct Tip {\n        address from;\n        uint256 amount;\n        uint256 timestamp;\n        string message;\n    }\n\n    IERC20 public immutable usdc;\n    address public immutable owner;\n\n    Tip[] public tips;\n    mapping(address => uint256) public totalTippedBy;\n    uint256 public totalTipped;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed from, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdraw(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error NotOwner();\n    error NothingToWithdraw();\n\n    modifier onlyOwner() {\n        if (msg.sender != owner) revert NotOwner();\n        _;\n    }\n\n    constructor(IERC20 _usdc, address _owner) {\n        usdc = _usdc;\n        owner = _owner;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Send a USDC tip with an optional message. The caller must first `approve` this contract\n     * for at least `amount` on the USDC token.\n     * @param amount USDC amount in base units (6 decimals, so 1 USDC == 1_000_000)\n     * @param message optional public message shown in the feed\n     */\n    function tip(uint256 amount, string calldata message) external {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        usdc.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n\n        tips.push(Tip({ from: msg.sender, amount: amount, timestamp: block.timestamp, message: message }));\n        totalTippedBy[msg.sender] += amount;\n        totalTipped += amount;\n\n        emit NewTip(msg.sender, amount, message, block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Owner withdraws the full USDC balance currently held by the jar.\n     */\n    function withdraw() external onlyOwner {\n        uint256 balance = usdc.balanceOf(address(this));\n        if (balance == 0) revert NothingToWithdraw();\n        usdc.safeTransfer(owner, balance);\n        emit Withdraw(owner, balance);\n    }\n\n    function tipsCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return tips.length;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Returns up to the most recent `count` tips, newest first — a bounded read for the UI feed.\n     */\n    function getRecentTips(uint256 count) external view returns (Tip[] memory) {\n        uint256 len = tips.length;\n        if (count > len) count = len;\n        Tip[] memory recent = new Tip[](count);\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n            recent[i] = tips[len - 1 - i];\n        }\n        return recent;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2306,"cache_read_input_tokens":47419,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2306,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"060da077-99cd-45e8-a32b-a8a6b07bee4d","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:58:08.705Z","request_id":"req_011CdMEgZmLToEKV4bNKtH3E"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMEiXYhGBA56YSisDLFK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013Pi5x4EsGhCRtQ5HXxfjFJ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.19;\n\nimport { Test } from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport { ERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { TipJar } from \"../contracts/TipJar.sol\";\n\ncontract MockUSDC is ERC20 {\n    constructor() ERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\") { }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 6;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\ncontract TipJarTest is Test {\n    MockUSDC internal usdc;\n    TipJar internal jar;\n\n    address internal owner = address(0xABCD);\n    address internal alice = address(0xA11CE);\n    address internal bob = address(0xB0B);\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1_000e6);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1_000e6);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address who, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRecordsAndTransfers() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10e6, \"gm\");\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 10e6);\n        assertEq(jar.tipsCount(), 1);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 10e6);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTippedBy(alice), 10e6);\n\n        (address from, uint256 amount,, string memory message) = jar.tips(0);\n        assertEq(from, alice);\n        assertEq(amount, 10e6);\n        assertEq(message, \"gm\");\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertOnZeroAmount() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        jar.tip(0, \"nope\");\n    }\n\n    function test_MultipleTipsAndRecentOrdering() public {\n        _tip(alice, 5e6, \"one\");\n        _tip(bob, 7e6, \"two\");\n        _tip(alice, 3e6, \"three\");\n\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 15e6);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTippedBy(alice), 8e6);\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory recent = jar.getRecentTips(2);\n        assertEq(recent.length, 2);\n        assertEq(recent[0].message, \"three\");\n        assertEq(recent[1].message, \"two\");\n    }\n\n    function assertEq(recent[0].message, \"only\");\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawOnlyOwner() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10e6, \"gm\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { TipJar } from \"../contracts/TipJar.sol\";\n\ncontract MockUSDC is ERC20 {\n    constructor() ERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\") { }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 6;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\ncontract TipJarTest is Test {\n    MockUSDC internal usdc;\n    TipJar internal jar;\n\n    address internal owner = address(0xABCD);\n    address internal alice = address(0xA11CE);\n    address internal bob = address(0xB0B);\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1_000e6);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1_000e6);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address who, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRecordsAndTransfers() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10e6, \"gm\");\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 10e6);\n        assertEq(jar.tipsCount(), 1);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 10e6);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTippedBy(alice), 10e6);\n\n        (address from, uint256 amount,, string memory message) = jar.tips(0);\n        assertEq(from, alice);\n        assertEq(amount, 10e6);\n        assertEq(message, \"gm\");\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertOnZeroAmount() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        jar.tip(0, \"nope\");\n    }\n\n    function test_MultipleTipsAndRecentOrdering() public {\n        _tip(alice, 5e6, \"one\");\n        _tip(bob, 7e6, \"two\");\n        _tip(alice, 3e6, \"three\");\n\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 15e6);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTippedBy(alice), 8e6);\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory recent = jar.getRecentTips(2);\n        assertEq(recent.length, 2);\n        assertEq(recent[0].message, \"three\");\n        assertEq(recent[1].message, \"two\");\n    }\n\n    function test_GetRecentTipsClampsToLength() public {\n        _tip(alice, 1e6, \"only\");\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory recent = jar.getRecentTips(100);\n        assertEq(recent.length, 1);\n        assertEq(recent[0].message, \"only\");\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawOnlyOwner() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10e6, \"gm\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NotOwner.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        jar.withdraw();\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(owner), 10e6);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawNothingReverts() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NothingToWithdraw.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_TipAccounting(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1_000e6);\n        _tip(alice, amount, \"fuzz\");\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), amount);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), amount);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTippedBy(alice), amount);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Reads the caller's USDC balance and the jar's\n * current allowance to decide whether to show \"Approve\" or \"Send tip\".\n */\nexport const TipForm = () => {\n  const { address: connectedAddress } = useAccount();\n  const { data: tipJar } = useDeployedContractInfo({ contractName: \"TipJar\" });\n  const tipJarAddress = tipJar?.address;\n\n  const [amount, setAmount] = useState(\"\");\n  const [message, setMessage] = useState(\"\");\n\n  const { data: usdcBalance } = useScaffoldReadContract({\n    contractName: \"USDC\",\n    functionName: \"balanceOf\",\n    args: [connectedAddress],\n  });\n\n  const { data: allowance, refetch: refetchAllowance } = useScaffoldReadContract({\n    contractName: \"USDC\",\n    functionName: \"allowance\",\n    args: [connectedAddress, tipJarAddress],\n  });\n\n  const { writeContractAsync: approveAsync, isMining: isApproving } = useScaffoldWriteContract({\n    contractName: \"USDC\",\n  });\n  const { writeContractAsync: tipAsync, isMining: isTipping } = useScaffoldWriteContract({\n    contractName: \"TipJar\",\n  });\n\n  let amountWei: bigint | undefined;\n  try {\n    amountWei = amount ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011LioiaQN9WMaBShA9BBVW4","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n2\t\n3\t<h4 align=\"center\">\n4\t  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n5\t  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n6\t</h4>\n7\t\n8\t🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n9\t\n10\t> [!NOTE]\n11\t> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n12\t\n13\t⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n14\t\n15\t- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n16\t- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n17\t- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n18\t- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n19\t- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n20\t\n21\t![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n22\t\n23\t## Requirements\n24\t\n25\tBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n26\t\n27\t- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n28\t- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n29\t- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n30\t\n31\t## Quickstart\n32\t\n33\tTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n34\t\n35\t1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n36\t\n37\t```\n38\tcd my-dapp-example\n39\tyarn install\n40\t```\n41\t\n42\t2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n43\t\n44\t```\n45\tyarn chain\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n49\t\n50\t3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n51\t\n52\t```\n53\tyarn deploy\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\tThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n57\t\n58\t4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n59\t\n60\t```\n61\tyarn start\n62\t```\n63\t\n64\tVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n65\t\n66\tRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n67\t\n68\t- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n69\t- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n70\t- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n71\t\n72\t\n73\t## Documentation\n74\t\n75\tVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n76\t\n77\tTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n78\t\n79\t## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n80\t\n81\tWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n82\t\n83\tPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"e39092c6-e2fe-4b76-b47e-9e6933c83394","timestamp":"2026-07-24T17:05:27.862Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/README.md","content":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n## Quickstart\n\nTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n\n1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n\n```\ncd my-dapp-example\nyarn install\n```\n\n2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n\n```\nyarn chain\n```\n\nThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n\n3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n\n```\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n\n4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n\n```\nyarn start\n```\n\nVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\nRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n\n- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n\n\n## Documentation\n\nVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n\nTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n\nPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","numLines":83,"startLine":1,"totalLines":83}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMFGUK7sgdDVGF78UMYg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QeNUfYXuWo2ySerWBJ7MgG","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/README.md","content":"# 💸 USDC Tip Jar (Base)\n\nA tip jar dApp for **Base**: a `TipJar` contract that accepts **USDC** tips\n(Base USDC `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`) with an optional public\nmessage, plus a frontend with a live tip feed and a send form (approve → tip).\n\nBuilt on Scaffold-ETH 2 (Foundry flavor). The SE-2 reference docs are further down.\n\n- **Contract:** `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol`\n- **Deploy script:** `packages/foundry/script/DeployTipJar.s.sol`\n- **Tests:** `packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol`\n- **Frontend:** `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx` + `packages/nextjs/components/tipjar/`\n- **Production / IPFS deploy:** see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md)\n\n---\n\n## Local development & demo — against **real Base state**, no real money at risk\n\nWe develop and demo everything on a **local fork of Base mainnet**. The fork is a\nthrowaway copy of real Base running on Anvil (chain id `31337`). The **real** USDC\ncontract lives at its real address on the fork, so demo tips are genuine USDC\ntransfers between real ERC-20 balances — but nothing touches mainnet and no real\nfunds are ever spent. When you kill the fork, all state disappears.\n\nThe `TipJar` is deployed with the real Base USDC address, and the frontend registers\nthe same USDC address for both the fork (`31337`) and Base (`8453`), so the app\nbehaves identically locally and in production.\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Node `>= v20` (Node 25 works; the IPFS build handles its `localStorage` quirk — see `DEPLOY.md`)\n- Yarn, Git, and [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil`, `cast`, `forge`)\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n### 1. Start a Base fork (Terminal 1)\n\n```bash\nyarn fork base\n```\n\nThis runs `anvil --fork-url base --chain-id 31337 --block-time 1` (the `base` RPC alias\nis defined in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`). `--block-time 1` mines a block every\nsecond so `block.timestamp` advances and the feed shows real times. The fork exposes\nthe RPC at `http://127.0.0.1:8545`.\n\n### 2. Deploy the TipJar to the fork (Terminal 2)\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nDeploys `TipJar(USDC, deployer)` and regenerates\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` (the frontend picks it up automatically).\n\n### 3. Start the frontend (Terminal 3)\n\n```bash\nyarn start\n```\n\nOpen `http://localhost:3000`. `scaffold.config.ts` targets `chains.foundry` (`31337`) —\nthe **fork's** chain id, not `chains.base`. Keep it on `foundry` for all local work.\n\n### 4. Seed test identities with real USDC, then demo\n\nThe demo moves **real USDC between two test identities**. We use the standard Anvil dev\naccounts as the identities (they're pre-funded with ETH for gas), and seed them with USDC\nby impersonating a Base USDC whale on the fork — a real USDC transfer that only exists on\nyour local fork.\n\n| Identity | Address | Private key (well-known Anvil dev key) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **Alice** | `0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266` | `0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80` |\n| **Bob** | `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8` | `0x59c6995e998f97a5a0044966f0945389dc9e86dae88c7a8412f4603b6b78690d` |\n\n**Seed both identities with USDC** (copy-paste; runs against the running fork):\n\n```bash\nexport ETH_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8545\nUSDC=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\n# A Base account that currently holds a large USDC balance (verify with the balanceOf line below).\nWHALE=0x20FE51A9229EEf2cF8Ad9E89d91CAb9312cF3b7A\nALICE=0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266\nBOB=0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8\n\n# Sanity-check the whale still holds USDC (should print a large number):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $WHALE\n\n# Give the whale gas, impersonate it, transfer real USDC to the test identities:\ncast rpc anvil_setBalance $WHALE 0xDE0B6B3A7640000          # 1 ETH for gas\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount $WHALE\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $ALICE 100000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  # 100 USDC\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $BOB    50000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  #  50 USDC\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount $WHALE\n\n# Confirm balances (USDC has 6 decimals, so 100 USDC == 100000000):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $ALICE\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $BOB\n```\n\n> **If the whale no longer holds USDC** (balances shift over time), pick any current holder\n> from [BaseScan USDC holders](https://basescan.org/token/0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913#balances)\n> and set `WHALE` to it. Anyone with a USDC balance works — you're only moving fork funds.\n\n**Drive the UI as each identity:** import Alice's / Bob's private key into MetaMask (or another\nwallet), add a network for `http://127.0.0.1:8545` with chain id `31337`, connect, and use the\nform: enter an amount + message → **Approve USDC** → **Send tip**. The tip appears in the feed\nfor everyone. (SE-2's burner wallet also works, but it generates a fresh empty account — seed it\nwith the whale step above using its address if you go that route.)\n\n**Or run the whole tip flow headless with `cast`** (no browser needed):\n\n```bash\nJAR=$(cast call --rpc-url $ETH_RPC_URL \\\n  $(jq -r '.transactions[0].contractAddress' packages/foundry/broadcast/Deploy.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json) 2>/dev/null || true)\n# Simpler: read the address from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address)\nJAR=<paste-TipJar-address>\nALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80\n\ncast send $USDC \"approve(address,uint256)\" $JAR 10000000 --private-key $ALICE_PK   # approve 10 USDC\ncast send $JAR  \"tip(uint256,string)\" 10000000 \"gm from Alice\" --private-key $ALICE_PK\n\ncast call $JAR \"totalTipped()(uint256)\"\ncast call $JAR \"getRecentTips(uint256)((address,uint256,uint256,string)[])\" 5\n```\n\n### 5. Run the contract tests\n\n```bash\nyarn foundry:test          # unit + fuzz tests for TipJar\n```\n\n---\n\n## How the contract works\n\n`TipJar` holds a fixed USDC token (set at deploy time) and an owner.\n\n- `tip(uint256 amount, string message)` — pulls `amount` USDC from the caller via\n  `safeTransferFrom` (caller must `approve` first), appends a `Tip` to the on-chain feed,\n  updates totals, and emits `NewTip`. Reverts on a zero amount.\n- `getRecentTips(uint256 count)` — newest-first, bounded read used by the UI feed.\n- `totalTipped`, `totalTippedBy(address)`, `tipsCount()` — running totals.\n- `withdraw()` — owner-only; sends the jar's full USDC balance to the owner.\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><h2 style=\"display:inline\">🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2 reference</h2></summary>\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: React hooks around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) for typed contract interactions.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers.\n\n### Requirements\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n> Note: this project uses `yarn fork base` (a Base mainnet fork) rather than the empty\n> `yarn chain`, because the tip jar needs the real USDC contract to exist. Use `yarn chain`\n> only if you specifically want an empty local chain with no tokens.\n\n### Documentation\n\nVisit the [SE-2 docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn more. To know more about its\nfeatures, check out the [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n### Contributing\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2! See\n[CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n\n</details>\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2782,"cache_read_input_tokens":85235,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2782,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"fedfc582-a38a-4cf8-80a8-8079551bba8b","timestamp":"2026-07-24T17:06:23.482Z","request_id":"req_011CdMFGSWDp7HYw6Xmm1vVB"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"64c22d98-27c0-498e-b32d-c0ad88958334","timestamp":"2026-07-24T17:06:23.512Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"update","filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/README.md","content":"# 💸 USDC Tip Jar (Base)\n\nA tip jar dApp for **Base**: a `TipJar` contract that accepts **USDC** tips\n(Base USDC `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`) with an optional public\nmessage, plus a frontend with a live tip feed and a send form (approve → tip).\n\nBuilt on Scaffold-ETH 2 (Foundry flavor). The SE-2 reference docs are further down.\n\n- **Contract:** `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol`\n- **Deploy script:** `packages/foundry/script/DeployTipJar.s.sol`\n- **Tests:** `packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol`\n- **Frontend:** `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx` + `packages/nextjs/components/tipjar/`\n- **Production / IPFS deploy:** see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md)\n\n---\n\n## Local development & demo — against **real Base state**, no real money at risk\n\nWe develop and demo everything on a **local fork of Base mainnet**. The fork is a\nthrowaway copy of real Base running on Anvil (chain id `31337`). The **real** USDC\ncontract lives at its real address on the fork, so demo tips are genuine USDC\ntransfers between real ERC-20 balances — but nothing touches mainnet and no real\nfunds are ever spent. When you kill the fork, all state disappears.\n\nThe `TipJar` is deployed with the real Base USDC address, and the frontend registers\nthe same USDC address for both the fork (`31337`) and Base (`8453`), so the app\nbehaves identically locally and in production.\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Node `>= v20` (Node 25 works; the IPFS build handles its `localStorage` quirk — see `DEPLOY.md`)\n- Yarn, Git, and [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil`, `cast`, `forge`)\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n### 1. Start a Base fork (Terminal 1)\n\n```bash\nyarn fork base\n```\n\nThis runs `anvil --fork-url base --chain-id 31337 --block-time 1` (the `base` RPC alias\nis defined in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`). `--block-time 1` mines a block every\nsecond so `block.timestamp` advances and the feed shows real times. The fork exposes\nthe RPC at `http://127.0.0.1:8545`.\n\n### 2. Deploy the TipJar to the fork (Terminal 2)\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nDeploys `TipJar(USDC, deployer)` and regenerates\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` (the frontend picks it up automatically).\n\n### 3. Start the frontend (Terminal 3)\n\n```bash\nyarn start\n```\n\nOpen `http://localhost:3000`. `scaffold.config.ts` targets `chains.foundry` (`31337`) —\nthe **fork's** chain id, not `chains.base`. Keep it on `foundry` for all local work.\n\n### 4. Seed test identities with real USDC, then demo\n\nThe demo moves **real USDC between two test identities**. We use the standard Anvil dev\naccounts as the identities (they're pre-funded with ETH for gas), and seed them with USDC\nby impersonating a Base USDC whale on the fork — a real USDC transfer that only exists on\nyour local fork.\n\n| Identity | Address | Private key (well-known Anvil dev key) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **Alice** | `0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266` | `0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80` |\n| **Bob** | `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8` | `0x59c6995e998f97a5a0044966f0945389dc9e86dae88c7a8412f4603b6b78690d` |\n\n**Seed both identities with USDC** (copy-paste; runs against the running fork):\n\n```bash\nexport ETH_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8545\nUSDC=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\n# A Base account that currently holds a large USDC balance (verify with the balanceOf line below).\nWHALE=0x20FE51A9229EEf2cF8Ad9E89d91CAb9312cF3b7A\nALICE=0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266\nBOB=0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8\n\n# Sanity-check the whale still holds USDC (should print a large number):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $WHALE\n\n# Give the whale gas, impersonate it, transfer real USDC to the test identities:\ncast rpc anvil_setBalance $WHALE 0xDE0B6B3A7640000          # 1 ETH for gas\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount $WHALE\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $ALICE 100000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  # 100 USDC\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $BOB    50000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  #  50 USDC\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount $WHALE\n\n# Confirm balances (USDC has 6 decimals, so 100 USDC == 100000000):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $ALICE\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $BOB\n```\n\n> **If the whale no longer holds USDC** (balances shift over time), pick any current holder\n> from [BaseScan USDC holders](https://basescan.org/token/0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913#balances)\n> and set `WHALE` to it. Anyone with a USDC balance works — you're only moving fork funds.\n\n**Drive the UI as each identity:** import Alice's / Bob's private key into MetaMask (or another\nwallet), add a network for `http://127.0.0.1:8545` with chain id `31337`, connect, and use the\nform: enter an amount + message → **Approve USDC** → **Send tip**. The tip appears in the feed\nfor everyone. (SE-2's burner wallet also works, but it generates a fresh empty account — seed it\nwith the whale step above using its address if you go that route.)\n\n**Or run the whole tip flow headless with `cast`** (no browser needed):\n\n```bash\nJAR=$(cast call --rpc-url $ETH_RPC_URL \\\n  $(jq -r '.transactions[0].contractAddress' packages/foundry/broadcast/Deploy.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json) 2>/dev/null || true)\n# Simpler: read the address from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address)\nJAR=<paste-TipJar-address>\nALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80\n\ncast send $USDC \"approve(address,uint256)\" $JAR 10000000 --private-key $ALICE_PK   # approve 10 USDC\ncast send $JAR  \"tip(uint256,string)\" 10000000 \"gm from Alice\" --private-key $ALICE_PK\n\ncast call $JAR \"totalTipped()(uint256)\"\ncast call $JAR \"getRecentTips(uint256)((address,uint256,uint256,string)[])\" 5\n```\n\n### 5. Run the contract tests\n\n```bash\nyarn foundry:test          # unit + fuzz tests for TipJar\n```\n\n---\n\n## How the contract works\n\n`TipJar` holds a fixed USDC token (set at deploy time) and an owner.\n\n- `tip(uint256 amount, string message)` — pulls `amount` USDC from the caller via\n  `safeTransferFrom` (caller must `approve` first), appends a `Tip` to the on-chain feed,\n  updates totals, and emits `NewTip`. Reverts on a zero amount.\n- `getRecentTips(uint256 count)` — newest-first, bounded read used by the UI feed.\n- `totalTipped`, `totalTippedBy(address)`, `tipsCount()` — running totals.\n- `withdraw()` — owner-only; sends the jar's full USDC balance to the owner.\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><h2 style=\"display:inline\">🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2 reference</h2></summary>\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: React hooks around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) for typed contract interactions.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers.\n\n### Requirements\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n> Note: this project uses `yarn fork base` (a Base mainnet fork) rather than the empty\n> `yarn chain`, because the tip jar needs the real USDC contract to exist. Use `yarn chain`\n> only if you specifically want an empty local chain with no tokens.\n\n### Documentation\n\nVisit the [SE-2 docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn more. To know more about its\nfeatures, check out the [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n### Contributing\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2! See\n[CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n\n</details>\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":83,"newStart":1,"newLines":182,"lines":["-# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2","+# 💸 USDC Tip Jar (Base)"," ","-<h4 align=\"center\">","-  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |","-  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>","-</h4>","+A tip jar dApp for **Base**: a `TipJar` contract that accepts **USDC** tips","+(Base USDC `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`) with an optional public","+message, plus a frontend with a live tip feed and a send form (approve → tip)."," ","-🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. See","+[CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).","+","+</details>"]}],"originalFile":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n## Quickstart\n\nTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n\n1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n\n```\ncd my-dapp-example\nyarn install\n```\n\n2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n\n```\nyarn chain\n```\n\nThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n\n3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n\n```\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n\n4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n\n```\nyarn start\n```\n\nVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\nRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n\n- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n\n\n## Documentation\n\nVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n\nTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n\nPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","userModified":false}}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"ec9faa9f-605e-43f2-b56b-685303d42398","timestamp":"2026-07-24T17:06:33.980Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/README.md","oldString":"```bash\nJAR=$(cast call --rpc-url $ETH_RPC_URL \\\n  $(jq -r '.transactions[0].contractAddress' packages/foundry/broadcast/Deploy.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json) 2>/dev/null || true)\n# Simpler: read the address from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address)\nJAR=<paste-TipJar-address>\nALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80","newString":"```bash\n# TipJar address — copy it from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address):\nJAR=<paste-TipJar-address>\nALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80","originalFile":"# 💸 USDC Tip Jar (Base)\n\nA tip jar dApp for **Base**: a `TipJar` contract that accepts **USDC** tips\n(Base USDC `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`) with an optional public\nmessage, plus a frontend with a live tip feed and a send form (approve → tip).\n\nBuilt on Scaffold-ETH 2 (Foundry flavor). The SE-2 reference docs are further down.\n\n- **Contract:** `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol`\n- **Deploy script:** `packages/foundry/script/DeployTipJar.s.sol`\n- **Tests:** `packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol`\n- **Frontend:** `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx` + `packages/nextjs/components/tipjar/`\n- **Production / IPFS deploy:** see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md)\n\n---\n\n## Local development & demo — against **real Base state**, no real money at risk\n\nWe develop and demo everything on a **local fork of Base mainnet**. The fork is a\nthrowaway copy of real Base running on Anvil (chain id `31337`). The **real** USDC\ncontract lives at its real address on the fork, so demo tips are genuine USDC\ntransfers between real ERC-20 balances — but nothing touches mainnet and no real\nfunds are ever spent. When you kill the fork, all state disappears.\n\nThe `TipJar` is deployed with the real Base USDC address, and the frontend registers\nthe same USDC address for both the fork (`31337`) and Base (`8453`), so the app\nbehaves identically locally and in production.\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Node `>= v20` (Node 25 works; the IPFS build handles its `localStorage` quirk — see `DEPLOY.md`)\n- Yarn, Git, and [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil`, `cast`, `forge`)\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n### 1. Start a Base fork (Terminal 1)\n\n```bash\nyarn fork base\n```\n\nThis runs `anvil --fork-url base --chain-id 31337 --block-time 1` (the `base` RPC alias\nis defined in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`). `--block-time 1` mines a block every\nsecond so `block.timestamp` advances and the feed shows real times. The fork exposes\nthe RPC at `http://127.0.0.1:8545`.\n\n### 2. Deploy the TipJar to the fork (Terminal 2)\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nDeploys `TipJar(USDC, deployer)` and regenerates\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` (the frontend picks it up automatically).\n\n### 3. Start the frontend (Terminal 3)\n\n```bash\nyarn start\n```\n\nOpen `http://localhost:3000`. `scaffold.config.ts` targets `chains.foundry` (`31337`) —\nthe **fork's** chain id, not `chains.base`. Keep it on `foundry` for all local work.\n\n### 4. Seed test identities with real USDC, then demo\n\nThe demo moves **real USDC between two test identities**. We use the standard Anvil dev\naccounts as the identities (they're pre-funded with ETH for gas), and seed them with USDC\nby impersonating a Base USDC whale on the fork — a real USDC transfer that only exists on\nyour local fork.\n\n| Identity | Address | Private key (well-known Anvil dev key) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **Alice** | `0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266` | `0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80` |\n| **Bob** | `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8` | `0x59c6995e998f97a5a0044966f0945389dc9e86dae88c7a8412f4603b6b78690d` |\n\n**Seed both identities with USDC** (copy-paste; runs against the running fork):\n\n```bash\nexport ETH_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8545\nUSDC=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\n# A Base account that currently holds a large USDC balance (verify with the balanceOf line below).\nWHALE=0x20FE51A9229EEf2cF8Ad9E89d91CAb9312cF3b7A\nALICE=0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266\nBOB=0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8\n\n# Sanity-check the whale still holds USDC (should print a large number):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $WHALE\n\n# Give the whale gas, impersonate it, transfer real USDC to the test identities:\ncast rpc anvil_setBalance $WHALE 0xDE0B6B3A7640000          # 1 ETH for gas\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount $WHALE\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $ALICE 100000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  # 100 USDC\ncast send $USDC \"transfer(address,uint256)\" $BOB    50000000 --from $WHALE --unlocked  #  50 USDC\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount $WHALE\n\n# Confirm balances (USDC has 6 decimals, so 100 USDC == 100000000):\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $ALICE\ncast call $USDC \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" $BOB\n```\n\n> **If the whale no longer holds USDC** (balances shift over time), pick any current holder\n> from [BaseScan USDC holders](https://basescan.org/token/0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913#balances)\n> and set `WHALE` to it. Anyone with a USDC balance works — you're only moving fork funds.\n\n**Drive the UI as each identity:** import Alice's / Bob's private key into MetaMask (or another\nwallet), add a network for `http://127.0.0.1:8545` with chain id `31337`, connect, and use the\nform: enter an amount + message → **Approve USDC** → **Send tip**. The tip appears in the feed\nfor everyone. (SE-2's burner wallet also works, but it generates a fresh empty account — seed it\nwith the whale step above using its address if you go that route.)\n\n**Or run the whole tip flow headless with `cast`** (no browser needed):\n\n```bash\nJAR=$(cast call --rpc-url $ETH_RPC_URL \\\n  $(jq -r '.transactions[0].contractAddress' packages/foundry/broadcast/Deploy.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json) 2>/dev/null || true)\n# Simpler: read the address from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address)\nJAR=<paste-TipJar-address>\nALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80\n\ncast send $USDC \"approve(address,uint256)\" $JAR 10000000 --private-key $ALICE_PK   # approve 10 USDC\ncast send $JAR  \"tip(uint256,string)\" 10000000 \"gm from Alice\" --private-key $ALICE_PK\n\ncast call $JAR \"totalTipped()(uint256)\"\ncast call $JAR \"getRecentTips(uint256)((address,uint256,uint256,string)[])\" 5\n```\n\n### 5. Run the contract tests\n\n```bash\nyarn foundry:test          # unit + fuzz tests for TipJar\n```\n\n---\n\n## How the contract works\n\n`TipJar` holds a fixed USDC token (set at deploy time) and an owner.\n\n- `tip(uint256 amount, string message)` — pulls `amount` USDC from the caller via\n  `safeTransferFrom` (caller must `approve` first), appends a `Tip` to the on-chain feed,\n  updates totals, and emits `NewTip`. Reverts on a zero amount.\n- `getRecentTips(uint256 count)` — newest-first, bounded read used by the UI feed.\n- `totalTipped`, `totalTippedBy(address)`, `tipsCount()` — running totals.\n- `withdraw()` — owner-only; sends the jar's full USDC balance to the owner.\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><h2 style=\"display:inline\">🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2 reference</h2></summary>\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: React hooks around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) for typed contract interactions.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers.\n\n### Requirements\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n> Note: this project uses `yarn fork base` (a Base mainnet fork) rather than the empty\n> `yarn chain`, because the tip jar needs the real USDC contract to exist. Use `yarn chain`\n> only if you specifically want an empty local chain with no tokens.\n\n### Documentation\n\nVisit the [SE-2 docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn more. To know more about its\nfeatures, check out the [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n### Contributing\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2! See\n[CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n\n</details>\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":114,"oldLines":9,"newStart":114,"newLines":7,"lines":[" **Or run the whole tip flow headless with `cast`** (no browser needed):"," "," ```bash","-JAR=$(cast call --rpc-url $ETH_RPC_URL \\","-  $(jq -r '.transactions[0].contractAddress' packages/foundry/broadcast/Deploy.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json) 2>/dev/null || true)","-# Simpler: read the address from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address)","+# TipJar address — copy it from packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts (TipJar.address):"," JAR=<paste-TipJar-address>"," ALICE_PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMFMM2hxN2LYvYVE8eAm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01E332CLZNAwcExWMd9ke9Ex","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T165411Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/DEPLOY.md","content":"# DEPLOY.md — Static IPFS build for the USDC Tip Jar\n\nThe site ships as a **static export on IPFS**. This document has the exact **build**,\n**upload**, and **post-deploy verification** commands. Nothing here uploads automatically —\nrun the steps deliberately.\n\nTwo things are deployed separately:\n\n1. **The `TipJar` contract** → Base mainnet (one-time, or already done).\n2. **The frontend** → a static bundle pinned on IPFS.\n\n---\n\n## 0. Prerequisites & config\n\n- Node `>= v20` (Node 25 is fine — the `localStorage` polyfill below handles it).\n- The production config in `packages/nextjs/`:\n  - `next.config.ts` already switches to a static export when `NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true`\n    (`output: \"export\"`, `trailingSlash: true`, `images.unoptimized: true`). Trailing slashes\n    are **required** so IPFS gateways resolve every route to a directory `index.html`\n    (without them, `/debug` → 404).\n  - `polyfill-localstorage.cjs` supplies the WebStorage methods Node 25 omits, injected into\n    **every** build worker via `NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\"`.\n    Without it, static prerendering crashes with `localStorage.getItem is not a function`.\n  - `scaffold.config.ts` already has `pollingInterval: 3000`.\n\n### Point the frontend at Base for production\n\nFor the live site the app must target **Base**, not the local fork. Set:\n\n```typescript\n// packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts\nimport * as chains from \"viem/chains\";\ntargetNetworks: [chains.base],\n```\n\nAlso set a real Base RPC (avoid the public `mainnet.base.org` in production) via an\n`rpcOverride` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALCHEMY_API_KEY` in `packages/nextjs/.env.local`:\n\n```typescript\nrpcOverrides: {\n  [chains.base.id]: \"https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/<YOUR_KEY>\",\n},\n```\n\n> Switch `targetNetworks` back to `[chains.foundry]` when you return to local fork development.\n\n---\n\n## 1. (If not already live) Deploy the TipJar contract to Base\n\n```bash\n# From repo root. Requires a funded deployer keystore (see `yarn account:import`).\nyarn deploy --file DeployTipJar.s.sol --network base\n```\n\nThis deploys `TipJar(0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, deployer)` and regenerates\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` with the Base (`8453`) address. Commit that file\nso the static build includes the real contract address.\n\nOptional verification on BaseScan:\n\n```bash\nyarn verify --network base\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Build the static bundle (exact command)\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nrm -rf .next out                      # ALWAYS clean first — avoids shipping a stale build\n\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://usdc-tipjar.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n```\n\n- `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` makes the OG/Twitter image an absolute URL instead of\n  `localhost` (see `utils/scaffold-eth/getMetadata.ts`). Set it to your final gateway URL.\n- Output is written to `packages/nextjs/out/`.\n\n### Verify the build BEFORE uploading\n\n```bash\n# Every route is a directory with an index.html (trailingSlash working):\nls out/index.html out/debug/index.html out/blockexplorer/index.html\n\n# OG image is absolute (your domain), NOT localhost:\ngrep -o 'property=\"og:image\"[^>]*' out/index.html\n\n# Page title is correct, not the stock SE-2 title:\ngrep -o '<title>[^<]*</title>' out/index.html          # -> <title>USDC Tip Jar</title>\n\n# The real TipJar address is baked into the JS (paste your Base TipJar address):\ngrep -rl \"<your-base-tipjar-address-without-0x>\" out/_next/static/chunks/ | head\n\n# Not stale — build output is newer than the source you changed:\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx\nstat -f '%Sm' out\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Upload to IPFS (exact command)\n\n```bash\n# Still in packages/nextjs. Uploads the ./out directory to BuidlGuidl IPFS.\nyarn bgipfs upload out\n```\n\nCopy the **CID** it prints. Your build is reachable at:\n\n```\nhttps://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>\n```\n\n> A real code change **always** produces a new CID. If the CID didn't change after you edited\n> code, you uploaded a stale `out/` — re-run step 2 (with `rm -rf .next out`) and try again.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Post-deploy verification (exact commands)\n\nReplace `<CID>` with the CID from step 3.\n\n```bash\nGATEWAY=\"https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>\"\n\n# 1. Home page loads (200):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"home:  %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/\"\n\n# 2. Routes resolve via trailing-slash directories (200, NOT 404):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"debug: %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/debug/\"\n\n# 3. OG metadata points at the production URL (not localhost):\ncurl -s -L \"$GATEWAY/\" | grep 'og:image'\n\n# 4. The page is the tip jar (matches on the H1 text):\ncurl -s -L \"$GATEWAY/\" | grep -o \"USDC Tip Jar\" | head -1\n```\n\nAll four must pass: `200`, `200`, an absolute `og:image` URL, and `USDC Tip Jar`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. (Optional) Point an ENS subdomain at the CID\n\nIf you're publishing under `usdc-tipjar.yourname.eth`, set its **content hash** to\n`ipfs://<CID>` in the [ENS app](https://app.ens.domains) (Records → Other → Content Hash),\nthen verify onchain and via the gateway:\n\n```bash\n# Content hash set onchain:\nRESOLVER=$(cast call 0x00000000000C2e074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e \\\n  \"resolver(bytes32)(address)\" $(cast namehash usdc-tipjar.yourname.eth) \\\n  --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com)\ncast call $RESOLVER \"contenthash(bytes32)(bytes)\" \\\n  $(cast namehash usdc-tipjar.yourname.eth) --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com\n\n# Gateway responds (allow 5–15 min for propagation) — use .eth.link (better on mobile):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" -L \"https://usdc-tipjar.yourname.eth.link\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Notes / gotchas\n\n- **Clean before every build** (`rm -rf .next out`). The #1 IPFS footgun is uploading a stale `out/`.\n- **`--require`, not `instrumentation.ts`:** the polyfill must load in the prerender worker\n  processes, which only `NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ...\"` guarantees.\n- **Custom OG thumbnail (optional):** the default `public/thumbnail.jpg` is the stock SE-2 image.\n  Replace it with a 1200×630 PNG/JPG before a public launch if you want a branded unfurl.\n- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true`** lets the static export finish past non-fatal type\n  checks; run `yarn check-types` separately to keep the code honest.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":714,"cache_read_input_tokens":91919,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":714,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"fdd305ee-c463-4217-92a5-2ec1f2e3ea82","uuid":"6f70cb42-1bd2-419e-a30d-7eff923541b5","timestamp":"2026-07-24T17:07:13.171Z","request_id":"req_011CdMFMKXfaCe8Hw9AhNHQ5"}
